name: Düğün Takip
subcategory: wedding planning, guest and gift tracking
tagline: A Turkish wedding planning tool for tracking guests, invitations, budget and gift money.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Under the wedding theming this is a guest list, an RSVP state machine, a budget ledger and a checklist. All four are textbook CRUD, and an agent can produce a working local version in one sitting including the gift money ledger that Turkish weddings actually need. The hard parts of a wedding are the relatives, not the data model. The one real argument for paying is that you use this for roughly four months and then never again, so building it yourself may cost more attention than it saves.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you add guests with side and table assignment, mark invited/confirmed/declined, log takı and cash gifts per guest, and track budget items against a total.
requirements: Node and a browser on your own machine
Willingness to run it locally or on a cheap VPS if your partner needs access
Manual entry of the guest list, there is no import from anywhere
whatYouLose: A phone-friendly app someone can actually use at the door on the wedding day without you babysitting a laptop
Shared access for your partner and family without you building auth or hosting
SMS and WhatsApp invitation sending, which needs a paid gateway either way
Prebuilt templates: seating layouts, vendor checklists, cost categories somebody already thought through
Backups and the certainty that the data is still there the week after the chaos
moatNotes: The only durable edges are a genuinely good mobile experience on the day and the messaging plumbing for invitations.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a wedding is a deadline you cannot move and the tool is disposable. Paying a small one-time or short-term fee for something that already has the checklist, the seating view, the phone app and the invitation sending beats spending a Saturday building a guest table while your budget spreadsheet rots. The product is not defensible in any technical sense; it is defensible because the customer has exactly one shot and no appetite for debugging.
notes: Rare case where the app wins on timing rather than moat: it is easy to clone and nobody planning a wedding wants to.
prompt:
Build a local-first wedding planning tracker. Stack: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, and SQLite via better-sqlite3. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry, no external APIs. Single user on localhost.

Data model, migrations run on boot:
- guests: id, full_name, phone, side (bride|groom|shared), group_label (family, work, neighbors, free text), invite_count, status (pending|invited|confirmed|declined), table_number, notes
- gifts: id, guest_id, kind (cash|gold|other), currency, amount, gold_unit (ceyrek, yarim, tam, gram), quantity, note, recorded_at
- budget_items: id, category, vendor, planned_amount, paid_amount, due_date, notes
- tasks: id, title, due_date, done, notes

Pages:
1. /guests : sortable and filterable table, inline status change, quick add row, search by name or phone, counts by status and by side in a sticky header, CSV export and CSV import with column mapping.
2. /gifts : per-guest gift entry form, running totals split by cash currency and by gold unit counts, no attempt to price gold, just counts.
3. /budget : budget item list with planned versus paid, remaining total, overdue payments highlighted.
4. /tasks : flat checklist with due dates, overdue first.
5. / : dashboard with confirmed headcount, total invite_count, gift totals, budget remaining, next five due items.

Rules: all UI labels in Turkish, all code and identifiers in English. Everything server-rendered with server actions, no client state library. Store the database file at ./data/wedding.db and put the path in .env as DATABASE_PATH. Add a /api/backup route that streams a copy of the db file.

Out of scope: sending SMS, WhatsApp or email, seating chart drag and drop, multi-user accounts, mobile app, gold price lookups. Do not add them.

Finish with a README: how to run, where the data lives, how to back it up, and one paragraph on how to add a seating view later.
